column1: #mapping_set_title: "Uniclass 2015 (verified codes) to ifcOWL IFC4 ADD2 crosswalk"

#comment: "Candidate-for-review crosswalk between Uniclass 2015 codes (verified against uniclass.thenbs.com, April 2026 table versions; see lift/uniclass_to_rdf.py) and ifcOWL IFC4 ADD2. Uniclass stratifies the built environment into tables (Complexes > Entities > Spaces > Elements > Systems > Products) while IFC types occurrences, so most correspondences here cross a strata boundary and say so. Rows with predicate_modifier=Not are asserted NON-mappings. SKOS direction per the SKOS Reference: A skos:broadMatch B asserts B is the broader concept; A skos:narrowMatch B asserts B is the narrower concept. Confidence is the curator's, not a computed score."

column9: comment
The cleanest element-level row. Residual gap: IFC splits curtain walling into IfcCurtainWall while EF_25_10 classifies the wall function regardless of construction.
Direct at the element level. IfcRoof is frequently a container aggregating slabs and beams; the EF code classifies the whole either way.

Crossed scopes rather than a clean match: IfcSlab is broader (it also serves as roof slab and landing, with a predefined type discriminating) and narrower (a floor element includes build-up beyond the structural slab). Kept at closeMatch because in exchange practice floor elements land as IfcSlab.
Decks (including bridge decks) have no dedicated IFC4 class; they are modelled as slabs by convention. Related, not close: IFC4 predates the infrastructure entities that would carry this properly.
Direct at the element level: both classify the door as an installed filling of an opening, and neither side splits doorsets from doors at this depth.
Direct at the element level, same shape as the doors row; IFC's IfcWindow likewise covers the window as installed opening filling.
Direct at the element level: IfcStair, like the EF code, denotes the whole vertical-circulation element and aggregates flights and landings beneath it.
Direct at the element level, mirroring the stairs row: IfcRamp aggregates ramp flights exactly as IfcStair aggregates stair flights.
Foundations is the broader function: IfcFooting carries the shallow-foundation case. Read as 'IfcFooting is the narrower concept'.
The deep-foundation case of the row above. IFC splits by construction method what Uniclass unifies by function; neither is wrong, and the crosswalk must carry both rows or silently lose piles.

IFC4 has no IfcCeiling class at all: ceilings are IfcCovering occurrences discriminated only by a CEILING predefined type. IfcCovering is the broader concept (it also carries claddings, floor coverings and wrappings), so this is a broadMatch with real information loss at the class level.

The stratification mismatch made explicit: Uniclass separates the wall element (EF_25_10) from the wall system (Ss_25), while a single IfcWall occurrence answers for both readings. One IFC class, two Uniclass strata. Any tool that maps IfcWall to exactly one Uniclass table has already made an undeclared modelling decision.
System-stratum counterpart of the EF door row; same conflation as Ss_25.
System-stratum counterpart of the EF window row.
System-stratum counterpart of the pile row: a piling system is the assembled set of piles plus caps and works, of which IfcPile occurrences are members.

The least losable and least clean row in the set: IFC4 has no frame entity, and an IfcElementAssembly instance can represent an assembled frame. Related only - most exchanged models represent frames as loose beams and columns with no assembly object at all.
System-stratum counterpart of the floors row, with the same crossed-scope caveats.
System-stratum counterpart of the ceilings row.

A space classification code names a kind of IfcSpace: the broader concept on the IFC side is the class, the Uniclass code is the discriminator. In a live model this row is realised as an IfcClassificationReference on the space, not as a class axiom - which is exactly why classification mappings survive every schema validator while carrying no checkable semantics.
An entity code names a kind of IfcBuilding. Same classification-not-axiom caveat as the SL row.

IFC4 has no complex entity; a campus-scale complex is approximated by IfcSite with compositionType COMPLEX, or by site aggregation. The Uniclass Complexes table simply has no first-class IFC4 counterpart, and this row is the closest honest anchor.

Table-level: Uniclass Ac classifies activities across the asset life cycle; IfcTask carries the scheduled-work case. Related, not close - Ac also classifies occupancy and operational activities that IFC represents nowhere.

Asserted non-mapping, and the canonical part-whole error of construction alignment: a beam is a part of a framed structure, not a kind of one. Tools infer 'frame maps to beam/column' from lexical overlap constantly, and because Uniclass asserts no axioms whatsoever, no reasoner and no SHACL shape will ever reject it. The mereology/taxonomy confusion must be refused by a human, here, in the record.

Asserted non-mapping at table level: Pr classifies products as supplied (the manufacturer's catalogue item); IfcElement is the installed occurrence in a building. The as-supplied/as-installed line is the construction twin of the as-designed/as-built line, and collapsing it makes every delivered pallet a wall. Products crosswalk to IfcElementType and material layers, each with loss, and that mapping is deliberately out of scope until it can be done per product group.
